speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and the location of these lesions, have you noticed any penile discharge or difficulty retracting the foreskin? I also need to ask if you have ever received the HPV vaccine or had any prior diagnoses of genital warts or pre-cancerous skin changes.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile and digital lesions. Given the patient's African origin, non-healing nature of the lesions, and lack of response to standard treatments, I suspect a condition like Erythroplasia of Queyrat or Bowen's disease, which are forms of squamous cell carcinoma in situ often associated with HPV.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any other skin lesions on sun-exposed areas, such as your face or hands, and do you have a history of genital warts? I am also noting your lack of response to previous syphilis treatment, which helps rule out infectious causes.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats, or malaise. No other similar lesions elsewhere on the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia and increased mitotic figures in the context of non-healing lesions are highly suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma in situ.
